questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the purpose of “Routing and Security”?
options: Routing and Security should be implemented by copying a snippet without checking the Angular version.
Routing and Security helps explain and implement one part of an Angular application; choose the API pattern that matches the behavior and verify it.
Routing and Security means the browser can enforce all permissions without the backend.
Routing and Security removes the need for error handling, accessibility checks and tests.
questions.answer_key: Routing and Security helps explain and implement one part of an Angular application; choose the API pattern that matches the behavior and verify it.
questions.explanation: Routing and Security is a concept in the supplied Angular curriculum. Its correct application depends on the intended behavior, surrounding context and verification.

questions.prompt: How should a learner work with “Authentication-aware navigation” in this lesson?
options: Connect “Authentication-aware navigation” to the lesson goal, use a focused example, and validate the behavior in the selected Angular environment.
Treat “Authentication-aware navigation” as a reason to skip the surrounding application context.
Assume “Authentication-aware navigation” works identically across every Angular major and runtime.
Use “Authentication-aware navigation” to bypass runtime validation of external or user-provided values.
questions.answer_key: Connect “Authentication-aware navigation” to the lesson goal, use a focused example, and validate the behavior in the selected Angular environment.
questions.explanation: The PDF explicitly lists “Authentication-aware navigation” under Routing and Security. Anchor it in a small example and check the behavior rather than relying on a memorized phrase.

questions.prompt: What is the strongest verification approach for “Routing and Security”?
options: Assume an SVG diagram proves the code compiled and passed tests.
Treat a successful client-side render as backend authorization evidence.
Ignore a failing test if the component looks correct in one browser.
Run the example in a compatible local Angular workspace, test the expected result and one failure case, and document any version limitation.
questions.answer_key: Run the example in a compatible local Angular workspace, test the expected result and one failure case, and document any version limitation.
questions.explanation: Verification evidence should match the running environment. Static teaching snippets are not compiler output, and frontend checks do not replace backend authorization.
